field_text:
Here is the Executive Summary of the Data Sharing Agreement (DSA):

This DSA, version 1.0.5, was created on November 14, 2025. The agreement involves two parties: OrgA, acting as the Data Controller, and OrgE, acting as the Recipient. The purposes of this DSA are analytics and fraud detection. The parties will process personal data, including biometric and contact information, based on legal bases of contract and public interest. The data will be stored for 12 months and disposed of securely after the agreement ends.

The DSA has a governance plan, incident response plan, and exit plan in place. The governance plan includes regular reviews every 12 months, with metrics such as breach MTTR (mean time to resolve) of less than 72 hours. The incident response plan includes a notification deadline of 72 hours and a contact point for reporting incidents.

The DSA also has an assessment, which concluded that the risk is low. The transparency arrangement includes a notice type of "layered" and an issuer of OrgA, with a procedure URL provided. The DSA has been reviewed and justified by a review note that recommends reducing the data categories processed.

Finally, the DSA has an international transfer arrangement in place, transferring personal data to Germany (DE) using standardized contractual clauses (SCCs) and encryption at rest, as well as access control.
label: Agreement metadata

field_text:
Here is the executive summary of the Data Sharing Agreement (DSA):

This DSA, version 1.0.1, was created on November 14, 2025. The agreement involves two parties: OrgB, acting as the data controller, and OrgC, acting as the processor. The purposes of this DSA are research and service provision. The legal bases for processing are public interest and legal obligation.

The agreement involves the use of two datasets: one containing location and biometric data, and another containing contact information. The retention period for the datasets is 18 months, with disposal method "Return". 

The rights handling procedures are in place for the right to erasure, with OrgB as the responsible party and a procedure URL provided. Transparency arrangements include direct notice to individuals, with OrgB as the issuer and a webpage providing further information.

The governance plan includes regular reviews every 12 months, with metrics for breach MTTR (mean time to respond) and audit rights on site annually. The incident response plan includes notification deadlines of 72 hours, with a contact point provided.

The exit plan outlines the procedures for exiting the agreement, including data disposition and post-termination obligations. The population covered by this DSA is employees.

Assessment information is available, including a TRA (Transparency Report) assessment outcome of "high" and references to a DPIA (Data Protection Impact Assessment).
label: Agreement metadata

field_text:
Here is the executive summary for the Data Sharing Agreement (DSA):

This DSA, version 1.0.0, was created on November 14, 2025. The agreement involves two parties: OrgA and OrgB, with OrgB acting as the Data Controller. The purposes of this DSA are reporting and service provision, with legal bases including a legal obligation and a contract. The data categories used or shared include location and biometric information.

The dataset, DSA_0003_DS1, conforms to a standard and will be stored for 18 months before being disposed of through return. The rights handling process, DSA_0003_RH1, is responsible for rectification and has a procedure URL. Transparency arrangements, DSA_0003_TA1, include layered notices issued by OrgB.

The governance plan, DSA_0003_Gov, includes regular reviews every 6 months and a third-party audit. The incident response plan, DSA_0003_IRP, requires notification within 72 hours and has a contact point. The exit plan, DSA_0003_Exit, includes secure deletion of data and no redisclosure after termination. The population covered by this DSA is general.

An assessment, DSA_0003_Assess, was conducted and found the risk to be high. The assessment report is available at <https://example.org/dpia.pdf>.
label: Agreement metadata

This DSA, version 1.0.1, was created on November 14, 2025. The agreement involves two parties: OrgC, acting as the Data Controller, and OrgE, acting as the Recipient. The purposes of this DSA are research and service provision. The legal bases for processing are a legal obligation and legitimate interest.

The DSA uses data categories related to location and health. The dataset, DSA_0033_DS1, conforms to a specific standard and will be stored for six months before being disposed of through anonymization. The international transfer of data to South Africa will be done through a business continuity and recovery service (BCRs) with safeguards in place, including access control and pseudonymization.

The rights handling procedure is responsible for the right to erasure, with OrgC being the responsible party and providing a procedure URL. Transparency arrangements include direct notice to individuals, with OrgC as the issuer and a webpage providing information.

The governance plan includes regular reviews every six months, with metrics such as breach mean time to recovery (MTTR) and audit rights for remote audits. The incident response plan includes a notification deadline of 72 hours, with contact information provided. The exit plan outlines the procedures for exiting the agreement, including secure deletion of data and no redisclosure obligations.

An assessment has been conducted, classified as low-risk, with a DPIA (Data Protection Impact Assessment) report available.

Transparency arrangements include direct notification to individuals and a webpage providing information on the DSA.

The agreement also includes an assessment, which concluded that there is a high risk of data breaches. The governance plan outlines review frequencies and metrics for monitoring compliance, while the incident response plan specifies notification deadlines and contact points. Finally, the exit plan outlines procedures for exiting the agreement, including data disposition and post-termination obligations.

This DSA includes enhanced safeguards to protect children's personal data, including age-appropriate design.

This DSA, version 1.0.4, was created on November 14, 2025. The agreement involves two parties: OrgC, acting as the Data Controller, and OrgE, acting as the Processor. The purposes of this DSA are service provision and research, with a legal basis of legitimate interest. The parties will process personal data categories including location and biometric information.

The DSA specifies that the processed data will be stored for six months, with a disposal method of return. The rights handling procedure includes the right to erasure, and the responsible party is OrgC.

The transparency arrangement requires indirect notice, with issuer OrgC and a procedure URL. The DSA has undergone an assessment, which concluded that the risk is low.

The governance plan includes regular reviews every six months, with a review metric of audit findings less than or equal to two. The incident response plan requires notification within 72 hours, with a contact point for security incidents.

The exit plan specifies that data will be disposed of securely upon contract end, with no obligation to redisclose the data. The population covered by this DSA is employees.

Here is the Executive Summary:

This Data Sharing Agreement (DSA) governs the sharing of personal data between two parties, OrgA and OrgB. The purposes of this DSA are fraud detection and service provision. The data categories involved include biometric, contact, and health information. The legal bases for processing are a legal obligation and contract.

The DSA has been assessed as having a low risk, with an assessment outcome of "low" and references to a Data Protection Impact Assessment (DPIA) available. The governance plan includes regular reviews every six months, with a metric to measure compliance and an audit right for remote audits.

In the event of an incident, OrgB will notify OrgA within 72 hours and provide a contact point for reporting incidents. The DSA also includes an exit plan, which outlines the procedures for disposing of personal data when the agreement ends. The plan includes a trigger for exit, which is the end of the contract, and a data disposition method of secure deletion.

The DSA has been implemented with safeguards in place to protect personal data, including the use of pseudonymization and key separation. International transfers of personal data will be made to Japan, with the use of standard contractual clauses (SCCs) and safeguards in place.

Incident response plans are in place, with a notification deadline of 72 hours and contact point provided.

Finally, an exit plan is in place, with triggers for contract end, data disposition of return, and post-termination obligations of no contact after exit. The population covered by this DSA is employees.

This DSA, version 1.0.1, was created on November 14, 2025. The agreement involves two parties: OrgB, acting as the Data Controller, and OrgC, acting as the Processor. The purposes of this DSA are research and service provision. The legal bases for processing are public interest and legal obligation.

The agreement involves the sharing of two datasets: one containing location and biometric data, and another containing contact information. The retention period for the datasets is 18 months, with disposal method "Return". The rights handling procedures are in place for erasure of personal data, and the responsible party is OrgB.

The governance plan includes regular reviews every 12 months, with a breach metric of "BreachMTTR<=72h". The incident response plan includes notification deadlines and a contact point. The exit plan outlines the procedures for exiting the agreement, including data disposal and post-termination obligations.

Assessment information is available, with an assessment type of "TRA" and outcome of "high". The DSA has undergone a transparency arrangement, with notice type "direct" and issuer OrgB.

This DSA, version 1.0.1, was created on November 14, 2025. The agreement involves two parties: OrgA, acting as the Data Controller, and OrgE, acting as the Recipient. The purposes of this DSA are reporting and service provision, with a legal basis of legitimate interest. The data categories used and shared include contact information and biometric data.

The dataset, DSA_0009_DS1, conforms to a standard and will be stored for 12 months before being disposed of through anonymization. The rights handling, DSA_0009_RH1, is managed by OrgA, and the transparency arrangement, DSA_0009_TA1, requires direct notice from OrgA.

The governance plan, DSA_0009_Gov, includes regular reviews every 12 months and remote audits. The incident response plan, DSA_0009_IRP, requires notification within 72 hours and contact through a specific email address. The exit plan, DSA_0009_Exit, includes secure deletion of data and no contact after the exit.

The population covered by this DSA is general, and an assessment has been conducted, with a low risk outcome. The assessment report can be found at <https://example.org/dpia.pdf>.

Finally, enhanced safeguards are in place to protect children's personal data, including age-appropriate design.

Here is the Executive Summary:

This Data Sharing Agreement (DSA) between OrgC and OrgD outlines the terms for sharing data between the two parties. The parties have agreed to review their governance plan every 12 months and conduct remote audits.

The DSA also includes an assessment, which concluded that the risks associated with this data sharing are low. The parties have agreed to implement enhanced safeguards, including age-appropriate design, to protect children's data.

Overall, this DSA outlines the terms for responsible and secure data sharing between OrgC and OrgD.

Here is the executive summary of the Data Sharing Agreement (DSA):

This DSA, version 1.0.3, was created on November 14, 2025. The agreement involves two parties: OrgE, acting as the Data Controller, and OrgA, acting as the Recipient. The purposes of this DSA are service provision and research, with legal bases grounded in legal obligation. The data categories involved include health and biometric information.

The DSA specifies that the shared dataset, DSA_0023_DS1, will be stored for 18 months and disposed of through anonymization. The rights handling process, DSA_0023_RH1, is responsible for rectification and handled by OrgE. Transparency arrangements, DSA_0023_TA1, require direct notice from OrgE.

The governance plan, DSA_0023_Gov, includes regular reviews every 12 months and audit rights for remote audits. The incident response plan, DSA_0023_IRP, requires notification within 72 hours and contact through email. The exit plan, DSA_0023_Exit, triggers data disposal upon contract end and prohibits contact after exit.

The population covered by this DSA is general, with no specific safeguards for child or vulnerable populations. An assessment, DSA_0023_Assess, has been conducted and is available at https://example.org/dpia.pdf.

field_text:
Here is the Executive Summary:

This Data Sharing Agreement (DSA) between OrgB and OrgD aims to facilitate data sharing for fraud detection and research purposes. The parties have defined specific roles, with OrgB acting as the Data Controller and OrgD as the Processor. The DSA purposes are to detect fraud and conduct research, with legal bases of legitimate interest and public interest respectively. The data categories used include contact information and health data.

The shared dataset, DSA_0024_DS1, conforms to a standard and will be stored for 12 months before being disposed of securely. The DSA includes an International Transfer arrangement with destination country "ZA" and transfer mechanism "Adequacy", with safeguards in place for key separation and pseudonymisation.

The DSA also includes arrangements for rights handling, transparency, and incident response. OrgB is responsible for handling the right to erasure, and a procedure URL has been provided. The DSA includes a transparency arrangement with notice type "indirect" and issuer OrgB.

Assessment information is also included, with an assessment outcome of "medium" and references to a Data Protection Impact Assessment (DPIA) report. The DSA includes governance, incident response, and exit plans, with review frequencies of 12 months and audit rights for on-site annual audits.

Overall, this DSA provides a framework for the sharing of personal data between OrgB and OrgD for specific purposes, with appropriate safeguards in place to protect the rights of individuals.

The agreement uses data categories related to health and biometric information.

Here is the executive summary of the Data Sharing Agreement (DSA):

This DSA, version 1.0.1, was created on November 14, 2025. The parties involved are OrgC, acting as the Data Controller, and OrgE, acting as the Recipient. The purposes of this DSA are research and service provision. The legal bases for processing are a legal obligation and legitimate interest.

The data categories used and shared include location and health information. The dataset, DSA_0033_DS1, conforms to a standard and will be stored for six months before being disposed of through anonymization. The international transfer of data to South Africa will be done through a business continuity and recovery service (BCRs) with safeguards in place, including access control and pseudonymization.

The rights handling procedures include the right to erasure, with OrgC responsible for implementing this procedure. Transparency arrangements are in place, including a notice type of "direct" and an issuer of OrgC. An assessment has been conducted, which concluded that the risks are low.

The governance plan includes regular reviews every six months and a metric for measuring breach response time. The incident response plan outlines procedures for notification and contact points. The exit plan includes triggers, data disposition, and post-termination obligations.

This DSA has been assessed as having a low risk profile.

This DSA, version 1.0.1, was created on November 14, 2025. The agreement involves two parties: OrgD, acting as the Data Controller, and OrgC, acting as the Processor. The purposes of this DSA are service provision and research, with legal bases including a legal obligation and public interest. The data categories involved are health and location.

The DSA specifies that the dataset will be stored for 18 months, with a disposal method of returning the data. The rights handling procedure is responsible to OrgD and includes procedures for erasure.

The transparency arrangement requires direct notice from the Data Controller, OrgD. The DSA has undergone an assessment, which concluded that there is a medium-level risk of data breaches. The governance plan includes regular reviews every 6 months, with metrics for breach response time and audit rights. The incident response plan requires notification within 72 hours, with a contact point for security incidents.

The exit plan specifies that data will be returned to the Data Controller upon contract end, with no obligation for further disclosure. The population covered by this DSA is employees.

Note that the assessment information, international transfer information, and child or vulnerable-population safeguards are not specified in this DSA.

The purposes of this DSA are analytics and reporting. The parties will process personal data categories including contact information and financial data, with legal bases of contract and public interest. The data will be stored for 12 months and disposed of securely.

The rights handling process is managed by OrgA, which will provide access to the data and maintain a procedure for handling requests. Transparency arrangements include direct notice from OrgA, with a review frequency of every 12 months.

The governance plan outlines the review frequency and audit rights, while the incident response plan includes notification deadlines and contact points. The exit plan specifies the trigger for termination, data disposition, and post-termination obligations.

The population covered by this DSA is employees.

Assessment information is also included, which indicates a medium-level risk assessment outcome and provides references to the Data Protection Impact Assessment (DPIA) report. Transparency arrangements are in place, including notice types and issuers.

Here is the Executive Summary for the Data Sharing Agreement (DSA):

This Data Sharing Agreement (DSA) between OrgB and OrgD outlines the terms for sharing data to support research and fraud detection purposes. The parties involved are OrgB, acting as the Data Controller, and OrgD, acting as the Processor. The DSA has been versioned to 1.0.2 and was created on November 14, 2025.

The purposes of the DSA are research and fraud detection, with legal bases established under public interest and legitimate interest. The data categories used and shared include contact information, location data, and financial data.

The dataset, DSA_0049_DS1, conforms to a specified standard and will be stored for 18 months before being disposed of using the SecureDelete method. Rights handling is managed by OrgB, which is responsible for rectification rights and has a procedure in place for handling these requests.

The transparency arrangement, DSA_0049_TA1, provides layered notice and is issued by OrgB. The governance plan, DSA_0049_Gov, outlines review frequencies and metrics for monitoring the agreement. The incident response plan, DSA_0049_IRP, includes notification deadlines and contact points for reporting incidents. The exit plan, DSA_0049_Exit, outlines the trigger and procedures for exiting the agreement.

The population covered by this DSA is employees.

This DSA, version 1.0.5, was created on November 14, 2025. The agreement involves two parties: OrgA, acting as the data controller, and OrgC, acting as the recipient. The purposes of this DSA are reporting and research, with legal bases established under contract law. The data categories involved include health and financial information.

The DSA specifies that the shared dataset, DSA_0050_DS1, will be stored for 12 months and disposed of through anonymization. The rights handling process, DSA_0050_RH1, ensures that the right to erasure is respected, with OrgA responsible for handling these requests. Transparency arrangements, DSA_0050_TA1, provide layered notices and are issued by OrgA.

The governance plan, DSA_0050_Gov, outlines regular review and audit processes to ensure compliance. The incident response plan, DSA_0050_IRP, includes a 72-hour notification deadline and contact information. The exit plan, DSA_0050_Exit, specifies that data will be returned to the controller upon contract termination. Finally, the population covered by this DSA is children, and enhanced safeguards are in place to ensure age-appropriate design.
label: Population, rights, and transparency

Here is the executive summary of the Data Sharing Agreement (DSA):

This DSA, version 1.0.2, was created on November 14, 2025. The agreement involves two parties: OrgC, acting as the Data Controller, and OrgE, acting as the Processor. The purposes of this DSA are analytics and fraud detection, with legal bases of legitimate interest and public interest. The data categories used and shared include financial and contact information.

The dataset, DSA_0051_DS1, conforms to a standard and will be stored for 18 months before being anonymized. The international transfer of data to South Africa (ZA) will be done through an adequacy mechanism, with safeguards in place for access control and encryption at rest.

The rights handling process includes procedures for erasure, with OrgC responsible for implementing these measures. Transparency arrangements include indirect notice and a webpage maintained by OrgC.

The governance plan, DSA_0051_Gov, outlines review frequencies and metrics for monitoring compliance. The incident response plan, DSA_0051_IRP, includes notification deadlines and contact points for reporting incidents. The exit plan, DSA_0051_Exit, outlines triggers and procedures for exiting the agreement.

The population covered by this DSA is employees. The assessment, DSA_0051_Assess, has identified a high risk and provides references to a data protection impact assessment (DPIA) report.

field_text:
Here is the executive summary of the Data Sharing Agreement (DSA):

This DSA, version 1.0.5, was created on November 14, 2025. The agreement involves two parties: OrgD, acting as the Data Controller, and OrgE, acting as the Recipient. The purposes of this DSA are service provision and reporting, with legal bases being contract and public interest. The data categories used and shared include location, health, contact information, and age.

The DSA specifies that the data will be stored for 12 months and then anonymized. The rights handling procedures are in place, including the right to erasure, with OrgD being responsible for this process. Transparency arrangements are also specified, including a notice type of "layered" and an issuer of OrgD.

The DSA has undergone an assessment, which concluded that the risk is low. The governance plan includes regular reviews every 6 months and audit rights for third-party auditors. In case of an incident, OrgE must notify OrgD within 72 hours and provide contact information. The exit plan specifies that data will be securely deleted when the contract ends, and there is no obligation to disclose personal data after termination.

Finally, this DSA has enhanced safeguards in place for children, including age-appropriate design.
label: Agreement metadata

This DSA, version 1.0.1, was created on November 14, 2025. The parties involved are OrgC (Data Controller) and OrgE (Recipient). Assessment information, DSA_0053_Assess, includes a DPIA assessment outcome of medium and references to a PDF document. International transfer information, DSA_0053_T1, includes destination country AU and transfer mechanism SCCs with safeguards of pseudonymization and access control.

The DSA population is children, and enhanced safeguards are in place to ensure age-appropriate design. An assessment has been conducted, with an outcome of "medium" and references to a Data Protection Impact Assessment (DPIA) report. Transparency arrangements are in place, including notice type "indirect" and issuer OrgB.

This DSA, version 1.0.0, was created on November 14, 2025. The parties involved are OrgA and OrgB, with OrgB acting as the Data Controller and OrgA as the Recipient. The purposes of this DSA are service provision and analytics, with legal bases being contract and public interest. The data categories used or shared include financial and location information.

The DSA specifies that the dataset will be stored for 18 months, with disposal method being anonymization. Rights handling is in place for rectification rights, with responsible party OrgB and procedure URL provided.

Transparency arrangements include layered notices issued by OrgB, with a review frequency of every 12 months. Governance plan details include review frequency, metrics, and audit rights.

In case of incidents, OrgB will notify the recipient within 72 hours. The exit plan specifies that data will be securely deleted upon contract end, with no redisclosure obligation.

This DSA applies to a general population.

field_text:
Here is the Executive Summary for the Data Sharing Agreement (DSA):

This Data Sharing Agreement (DSA) between OrgB and OrgE enables the sharing of data for analytics and reporting purposes. The agreement's primary purpose is to support OrgB's role as a data controller, while OrgE acts as the recipient of the shared data. The DSA covers two processing activities: one for analytics and another for reporting, both of which use location and health data categories. The agreement specifies that the shared dataset will be stored for 12 months before being disposed of through return. The rights handling process is managed by OrgB, which is responsible for erasure requests and has a procedure in place for handling such requests. Transparency arrangements include indirect notice provision by OrgB, and the agreement has undergone a Data Protection Impact Assessment (DPIA) with an outcome of "high". The governance plan outlines review frequencies, metrics, and audit rights, while the incident response plan specifies notification deadlines and contact points. Finally, the exit plan outlines triggers, data disposition, and post-termination obligations.

Note: The assessment information is explicitly mentioned in the TTL input.

OrgE has a rights handling procedure for data subjects' right to erasure, which is responsible by OrgE and can be accessed at <https>.

OrgE has a transparency arrangement for direct notice to data subjects, issued by OrgE and accessible at <https>.

OrgE has conducted a DPIA assessment with an outcome of low risk and references <https://example.org/dpia.pdf>.

OrgE has a governance plan with a review frequency of six months, a metric of BreachMTTR<=72h, and an audit right of remote_audit.

OrgE has an incident response plan with a notification deadline of 72 hours and a contact point of mailto:sec@example.org.

OrgE has an exit plan with an exit trigger of contract_end, data disposition of return, and a post-termination obligation of no contact after exit.

OrgE has a population of children, which is shared with the DSA.

OrgE has an enhanced safeguard of age-appropriate design.

The DSA includes a review note justifying the processing activity of fraud detection, which references ICO-2021-§3.2 and has a decision of needs-change with a rating of 2. The description is "reduce data categories".

The Data Sharing Agreement (DSA) between OrgE and OrgB involves two parties: OrgE as the Data Controller and OrgB as the Recipient. The DSA has two purposes: fraud detection and service provision.

The agreement includes a governance plan, an incident response plan, and an exit plan. The governance plan involves reviewing the agreement every six months, measuring breach mean time to repair (MTTR) and conducting remote audits. The incident response plan requires notifying OrgE within 72 hours of any breach and contacting them at sec@example.org. The exit plan involves returning the data to OrgE upon contract termination and prohibiting redisclosure.
